name: Edom, in the day of his brother
charge: Standing on the other side when strangers carried Jacob away; rejoicing over Judah's fall; cutting off those that escaped
summary: When Babylon took Jerusalem, Esau's descendants looked on, entered the gate in the day of calamity, laid hands on the substance, stood in the crossway to cut off the fugitives, and delivered up those that remained. Psalm 137 remembers them shouting, rase it, rase it, even to the foundation.
offense: Edom's pride rested in its mountain strongholds, but its offense was also betrayal of its brother Jacob. When strangers carried away Jerusalem's forces, Edom stood on the other side and was as one of them. It rejoiced over Judah's destruction, entered the gate to take spoil, and stood at the crossroads to cut off those escaping and deliver up survivors. The calamity of a brother became an opportunity for gain. Neither distance from the original invasion nor the strength of its rock dwellings made Edom innocent of what it did to the defeated and fleeing.
judgment: The Lord declared that He would bring Edom down even from a nest set among the stars. Its confederates would deceive it, its wisdom would fail, and its mighty men would be dismayed. The recompense followed its conduct: as it had done, it would be done unto it. Obadiah set this overthrow beside deliverance upon mount Zion and the possession of their inheritance by the house of Jacob. The kingdom would be the Lord's. Edom's expectation of profiting from Judah's fall could not prevail over God's judgment of its violence or His purpose for restoration.

verses.text: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.

But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.

Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.
Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them;

Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword.

And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.
Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:
Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.
Thus will I make mount Seir most desolate, and cut off from it him that passeth out and him that returneth.
And I will fill his mountains with his slain men: in thy hills, and in thy valleys, and in all thy rivers, shall they fall that are slain with the sword.
I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever:
But I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.
Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.
I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob,
And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother: thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian; because thou wast a stranger in his land.
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.
The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.

text.text: For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.
For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.
But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.

entries.commentary: The vision of Obadiah, and it is spoken concerning Edom: Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle. Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.

If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, would they not have stolen till they had enough? If the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes? But Esau is searched out, and his hidden things sought up. All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border; the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee. They that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee. Shall I not in that day destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.

For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them. Esau stood on the other side and took part. Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance; neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway to cut off those of his that did escape, nor have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.

For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head. As ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually; they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions. The house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble; and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau, for the Lord hath spoken it. They of the south shall possess the mount of Esau, and they of the plain the Philistines; and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria; and Benjamin shall possess Gilead. Saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord's. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom)

The word of the Most High comes against the Ammonites, the so-called Japanese, because they said Aha against His sanctuary when it was profaned, against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity. Because they clapped their hands, stamped their feet, and rejoiced in heart with all their despite against Israel, cheering our destruction, He will deliver them to the men of the east for a possession, cut them off from the people, and cause them to perish, that they may know He is the Lord.

Because Moab, the so-called Chinese, and Seir say that the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen, claiming Judah is no longer the Most High's chosen people, judgment is pronounced against them. The Most High will open the side of Moab from his frontier cities, the glory of the country, and deliver them to the men of the east along with the Ammonites so that the Ammonites be not remembered among the nations, and He will execute judgments upon Moab.

Because Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance and greatly offended, the Most High will stretch out His hand upon Edom, cut off man and beast, and make it desolate from Teman, and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands. -

Because the Philistines dealt by revenge and took vengeance with a despiteful heart to destroy for the old hatred, never letting the feud go the way they always warred with us from the days of the judges, Samuel, Saul, and David, judgment comes upon them. The Most High will stretch out His hand upon the Philistines, cut off the Cherethims, destroy the remnant of the sea coast, and execute great vengeance with furious rebukes, that they may know He is the Lord when He lays His vengeance upon them.

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

The gold has become dim and the most fine gold changed; the stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the top of every street, and the precious sons of Zion, once comparable to fine gold, are now esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the potter's hands. Even the sea monsters draw out the breast and give suck to their young, but the daughter of the people is become cruel like the ostrich in the wilderness; the tongue of the suckling cleaves to the roof of his mouth for thirst, and the young children ask bread and no man breaks it to them. They that fed delicately are desolate in the streets, and they that were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills, for the punishment of the iniquity of the people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment. The famine of the siege was so severe that a nation once raised in the finest things was reduced to nothing, and their judgment for their sin exceeded even the sin of Sodom.

Her Nazarites were purer than snow, whiter than milk, more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing of sapphire, but their visage is now blacker than a coal, and they are not known in the streets. The verse says their visage is blacker than a coal, which shows plainly that the Israelites are a black people; the coal is the natural color of the nation and the burning of the famine only made it darker. They that are slain with the sword are better than they that are slain with hunger, for these pine away, stricken through for want of the fruits of the field. The hands of the pitiful women sodden their own children for meat in the destruction of the people, and the Most High accomplished His fury and poured out His fierce anger, kindling a fire in Zion that devoured its foundations.

The kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed that the adversary and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem, but it came to pass for the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests that shed the blood of the just in her midst. They wandered as blind men in the streets, polluted with blood so that men could not touch their garments, and the people cried unto them, Depart, it is unclean, depart. The anger of the Most High divided them and He would no more regard them; they respected not the persons of the priests and favored not the elders, for the leadership that was supposed to guide the people had defiled itself.

Their eyes failed watching for a vain help; they watched for a nation that could not save them, looking to other countries to deliver them instead of to the Most High. Their persecutors were swifter than the eagles of heaven, pursuing them upon the mountains and laying wait for them in the wilderness, so that they could not go in their streets and their end was come. The breath of their nostrils, the anointed of the Most High, was taken in their pits, the very one under whose shadow they thought to live among the heathen.

Edom is told to rejoice and be glad in the land of Uz, but the cup shall pass through unto her also; she shall be drunken and make herself naked, for her turn of judgment is coming. The punishment of the iniquity of Zion is accomplished and the Most High will no more carry her away into captivity, but He will visit the iniquity of Edom and discover her sins.
